ideas.name: SilverScale
ideas.niche: Precision exposure compensation for non-standard film ISOs and vintage optics.
ideas.problem: The high financial risk of wasting expensive specialty or expired film due to manual math errors when calculating exposure for pushed/pulled film or compensating for vintage lens metering inconsistencies.
ideas.targetUser: Analog photography enthusiasts and professionals (ages 18-45) who utilize manual SLR/Rangefinder cameras and frequently use specialty stocks like Cinestill, expired rolls, or underexposed film.
coreFeatures: ISO Push/Pull Engine: Rapidly calculate stop compensation for specific push/pull increments.
Expired Film Decay Estimator: Adjusts exposure values based on estimated age and storage temperature profiles.
Vintage Lens Profile Library: Presets to compensate for known light-leak or metering variances in specific vintage glass.
Tactile Stop-Value Slider: A high-contrast, large-target UI slider for rapid 1/3 or 1/2 stop adjustments in field conditions.
realDependencies: Cloud-hosted Film Stock Database (to update new film releases)
User Profile Sync (Firebase/Supabase) for custom film/lens presets
Mobile Device Ambient Light Sensor API for real-time light metering
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local 'MockDataRegistry' JSON object containing a library of 100+ film stocks (Kodak, Fujifilm, Ilford) and lens profiles. All 'network' requests will be handled by an asynchronous wrapper function that uses `setTimeout` to inject a random 400ms-1500ms delay, simulating API latency. The light sensor will be emulated via a 'Simulated Environment' menu where the user selects a state (e.g., 'Golden Hour', 'Deep Shade'), which then feeds static lux values into the calculation engine. Authentication will be mocked with a hardcoded successful redirect after a simulated 1-second loading spinner.

ideas.name: Flux
ideas.problem: Executive dysfunction and task initiation paralysis caused by the 'invisibility' of time and the overwhelming nature of long-duration timers.
ideas.targetUser: Neurodivergent professionals and students (ages 18-40) experiencing 'waiting mode' or difficulty transitioning between tasks due to dopamine-seeking distractions.
coreFeatures: Shrink-Scale Geometry: A geometric shape that physically contracts or dissolves in real-time to represent time remaining
Chroma-Urgency: High-contrast color transitions (e.g., teal to vibrant amber) to signal urgency without auditory stimulation
One-Tap Micro-Sprints: Pre-set 5, 10, and 15-minute bursts to bypass decision fatigue during task initiation
Dopamine Visualizers: Subtle, non-distracting particle animations upon completion to provide immediate task-completion reward
Zero-Text Mode: A minimalist UI that removes all distracting labels, focusing solely on the visual countdown
realDependencies: Firebase Auth and Firestore for user session history
Native iOS/Android Haptic Feedback APIs for tactile urgency
Local Push Notification Service for session end alerts
Apple HealthKit/Google Fit integration for focus-to-rest correlation
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will implement a 'MockServiceLayer' to intercept all external calls. Firebase will be replaced by a local `MockDB` object that uses `setTimeout` to simulate realistic 800ms-1200ms network latency for all CRUD operations. Native Haptics will be emulated via a `ConsoleHapticLogger` and a temporary CSS 'shake' animation on the UI container. Local Notifications will be redirected to an in-app 'Toast' notification system. To facilitate rapid testing of the time-sensitive visual components, a `TimeController` will be provided to allow the developer to 'warp' time by a 10x multiplier during the simulation.

ideas.name: GutCheck
ideas.niche: Real-time qualitative client risk assessment for freelance discovery calls.
ideas.problem: Freelancers often ignore subtle behavioral warning signs during high-pressure sales calls, leading to 'nightmare clients' and scope creep due to optimism bias.
ideas.targetUser: Independent creative and technical freelancers (ages 22-45) who manage their own discovery calls and struggle with objective decision-making during live negotiations.
coreFeatures: One-Tap Stealth Tally: A minimalist, low-distraction interface to log flags without looking away from the client.
Client Risk Scoring: A real-time algorithm that converts tap frequency into a 'Go/No-Go' probability score.
Post-Call Debrief: Auto-generates a structured summary of red flags for quick reference during contract drafting.
Pattern Recognition: A historical dashboard that tracks recurring red-flag themes across all past leads.
realDependencies: OpenAI API (To turn tally patterns into written debriefs)
ideas.emulationStrategy: Use a local MockData repository to provide static user and flag history. Implement a 'MockNetwork' wrapper that intercepts all API calls, applies a variable delay (800ms–2500ms) to simulate server latency, and returns hardcoded JSON responses. The AI-generated report will be emulated by a template function that parses the counts of specific flag types and injects them into a pre-written professional summary string. Subscription logic will be bypassed via a 'Developer Bypass' toggle that mimics a successful Stripe webhook.

ideas.name: VoltVoyage
ideas.problem: Risk of permanent device damage and travel friction caused by incompatible plug types and voltage mismatches in foreign countries.
ideas.targetUser: Frequent international travelers, digital nomads, and business professionals carrying sensitive electronic equipment across multiple global borders.
coreFeatures: Instant Country Search with high-resolution visual plug type identification
Voltage & Frequency mismatch alerts (Dual-voltage vs. Single-voltage warnings)
Device-to-Country Compatibility Checker (Input device specs to get safety status)
Offline Mode with cached global electrical standards
realDependencies: GeoIP/Location Services API for automatic country detection
RESTful API for real-time standard updates
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local 'mock_database.json' containing a curated dataset of 200+ countries with mapped plug types (A-N), voltage, and frequency. A 'MockService' wrapper will intercept all data requests, using 'setTimeout' to inject variable network latency (400ms to 1200ms) to mimic real API calls. Location detection will be emulated through a 'Simulate Current Location' toggle that overrides the browser's geolocation with specific country coordinates. Search functionality will perform a case-insensitive fuzzy match against the local JSON to simulate a server-side search endpoint. To test robustness, a 'Chaos Mode' toggle will be included to randomly trigger simulated 500-series error responses.

ideas.name: Syncro
ideas.problem: The cognitive load and scheduling errors caused by manual mental math when attempting to coordinate synchronous meetings across extreme global time differences.
ideas.targetUser: Location-independent remote workers, distributed team leads, and freelance consultants who manage clients and collaborators across multiple continents.
coreFeatures: Multi-Zone Synchronized Sliders
Visual 'Golden Window' Overlap Heatmap
One-Tap Meeting Invite Text Generator
Real-Time Calendar Conflict Detection
ideas.emulationStrategy: Implement a 'MockService' interceptor that replaces all external fetch requests. Use a local JSON manifest mapping 50 major global cities (e.g., Bali, London, NYC, Tokyo) to IANA time zone strings to bypass Geocoding. Every 'API' response will be wrapped in a Promise that resolves after a randomized delay between 500ms and 1500ms to simulate network latency. Calendar data will be simulated by returning a static array of 'Event' objects with timestamps dynamically calculated to appear as 'busy' blocks in the current week.
